newsitem.title: USA: Florida tobacco liability trial delayed.
newsitem.headline: Florida tobacco liability trial delayed.

text.p: A Florida judge on Wednesday ordered a delay of at least six months in the trial of a tobacco liability case in which a smoker seeks damages from cigarette maker Liggett Group for his cancer.
Duval County Circuit Judge Charles Mitchell granted a motion filed by attorneys for James Clark, 51, to postpone a trial that was scheduled to start on Monday.
Clark filed a product liability lawsuit against Liggett, a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, blaming his lung and brain cancer on the company's L&M cigarettes.
The trial will be rescheduled no earlier than April 14, Mitchell ruled, adding that a gag order on all parties in the case remained in effect.
The order did not cite a reason for the delay but Clark's wife 28 years, Betty Clark, said her husband is ill.
Postponing the trial "gives us more time right now, and we need the quiet time together," Betty Clark said.
